question: What is the isolation sequence before opening the CAPPER turret guard?
guidelines: Lists the seven steps in order, electrical isolation before pneumatic.
States that the pneumatic accumulator must be vented, and why: the turret can index once on stored air.
States that zero energy is verified by attempting a start before the guard is opened.
Cites SOP-CAP-021.

question: What fill target and low-fill alarm do I set when changing the FILLER over to 1.0 L?
guidelines: Gives 1000 ml target and 988 ml low-fill alarm.
Mentions restarting at 180 BPM before going to the nominal 420 BPM.
Mentions the ten verification bottles within 1000 ml plus or minus 6 ml.
Cites SOP-FILL-014.

question: The CAPPER application torque is reading 18 Nm. What does that cause downstream?
guidelines: States the working window is 20 to 24 Nm, nominal 22 Nm.
Explains low torque gives loose caps and leaks seen as under-weight cases at the CHECKWEIGHER.
Does not claim low torque causes cracked caps; that is the high-torque failure.

question: Why did the LABELLER reject rate spike on the night of 14 March, and what was done about it?
guidelines: Root cause is cold adhesive added mid-shift pulling glue temperature below the 165 to 175 °C window.
Mentions the logged 158 to 161 °C and the skewed labels.
Lists the corrective actions including the 163 °C low alarm.
Cites deviation DEV-2026-03-011.

question: The line has been stopped at the FILLER for ten minutes. What do I do with the bottles in the PASTEURIZER?
guidelines: States that bottles held longer than four minutes at setpoint exceed 26 PU and must be diverted.
Says to drop zone 2 to 55 °C and return to 68 °C before restarting.
Gives the 18 to 26 PU target.
Cites SPEC-PAS-003.

question: Did closure lot 2026-04-221 pass, and does it need a torque change on the CAPPER?
guidelines: States every characteristic passed.
States no machine adjustment is needed; the lot is qualified for 22 Nm.
Notes liner thickness at 1.17 mm is in the lower half of the window and to check torque heads first if caps are loose.

question: CONVEYOR_2 accumulation pressure is above 80 % while the FILLER is stopped. Is the conveyor faulty?
guidelines: Says this is the buffer doing its job, not a conveyor fault, and to check the FILLER first.
Gives the normal 30 to 70 % accumulation range.
Mentions infeed jams at the FILLER handover as the consequence of sustained high pressure.

question: How long can a machine be stopped before the line loses cases?
guidelines: States each accumulation conveyor holds about four minutes of production at nominal rate.
Explains downstream starves and upstream blocks, and that below 60 % buffer level capacity starts to fall.
Concludes a stop shorter than about four minutes shows as a rate dip rather than lost cases.

question: What zone 2 temperature and PU window should I run the PASTEURIZER at?
guidelines: Answers 68 °C and 18 to 26 PU, from SPEC-PAS-003 revision 3.
States that technical bulletin TB-2026-05 proposes 69 °C and 20 to 30 PU but is NOT approved, so it does not apply.
Names the specification as governing where the two disagree.
Does not present the bulletin's numbers as current.

question: Why is the 1.0 L format packed at 400 BPM instead of the line nominal 420?
guidelines: Explains the CASE_PACKER is rated to 30 cases per minute and 12-packs at 420 BPM would need 35.
States the FILLER pacemaker is deliberately slowed to protect the downstream machine.
Cites SPEC-FILL-021.

question: We are changing from cola to the dairy-protein shake. What cleaning is required?
guidelines: Group C to group D requires a full clean in place, the six-phase SOP-CIP-002 sequence, about 64 minutes plus heat-up.
States that protein verification is required on the way OUT of group D, not into it.
Mentions that group D is the only allergen-bearing group, milk.
Cites the cleaning matrix.

question: How long should I plan for a 0.5 L to 1.5 L changeover, and what is on the critical path?
guidelines: Gives 85 minutes as the line critical path.
States the FILLER is the critical path at 75 minutes, carousel work.
Notes the CAPPER is not on the critical path because all three formats use the same 28 mm closure.
Mentions the delivered pasteurisation check before releasing the run.

question: The EMPTY_INSPECTOR reject rate has climbed to 4 per minute. Where do I look?
guidelines: States normal is below 2 per minute at 420 BPM.
Directs the reader by reject type: residue film points at BOTTLE_WASHER caustic temperature or concentration, residual liquid at rinse drainage or tunnel speed.
Mentions rejects concentrated in one lane are mechanical.
Does not treat a high reject rate as an EMPTY_INSPECTOR fault by default.

question: What happened on the 18 April day shift, and was any product destroyed?
guidelines: Reports the seven-minute CAPPER cap chute stop at 09:42.
States 240 bottles in the PASTEURIZER were diverted and destroyed as over-pasteurised, because the four-minute limit was exceeded.
Mentions zone 2 was dropped to 55 °C and returned to 68 °C before restart.
Cites batch record BR-2026-0418-A.

question: Which checks on this line are critical control points, and what happens if one fails?
guidelines: Names the three: PASTEURIZER delivered PU, CAPPER application torque, EMPTY_INSPECTOR foreign object.
Gives the critical limits: 18 to 26 PU, 20 to 24 Nm, no object above 2 mm.
Explains the quarantine boundary is back to the last passed check, so check frequency sets quarantine size.
Cites the HACCP plan.

question: The FILLER fill average looks fine but one group of valves is inconsistent. Does that matter?
guidelines: States valves 13 to 18 were 3.6 ml low as-found with more than double the spread, and two worn valve seals were replaced.
Explains the spread was the signal rather than the mean, because bowl level control compensates for a weeping seal.
Mentions the recommendation to shorten the seal interval to four months for that group.
Cites the calibration certificate.

question: The CASE_PACKER keeps jamming on carton feed. What caused this last time?
guidelines: Root cause was wet lubricant applied at the CONVEYOR_3 discharge, migrating onto carton blanks.
States the maintenance manual permits dry lubricant at transfer plates only.
Notes the jam presents three machines away from the cause, which is why it took two weeks to find.
Cites the root cause analysis.

question: Caustic temperature fell at the BOTTLE_WASHER and zone 2 fell at the PASTEURIZER at the same time. Two faults?
guidelines: States both are fed from the same plant room hot water and steam loop, so one upstream cause is more likely than two faults.
Says to check the shared supply before treating either machine as faulty.
May note the same pattern was recorded in the week 16 handover log on 16 April.

question: What is the caustic phase temperature and duration in the wet end clean in place?
guidelines: Gives 75 to 80 °C at 1.8 to 2.2 % for 20 minutes.
States the total circuit is about 64 minutes plus heat-up.
Notes shortening the caustic phase is the most common cause of a failed hygiene swab.
Gives the release criteria including swabs below 150 relative light units.
